big_story.headline: US Proposes 25% Tariffs on India
big_story.subhead: NEW WASHINGTON TRADE PROPOSALS TARGET INDIA AND 13 OTHER PARTNERS WITH HIGH DUTIES
paragraphs: The United States has proposed new import tariffs of up to 25% on India, alongside 13 other international trade partners. The sudden proposal marks a sharp turn in Washington's trade policy, creating fresh uncertainty for cross-border commerce. Industry groups are closely analyzing the potential impact on major export sectors that rely heavily on American demand.

The move signals renewed protectionist measures designed to shield domestic American industries from international competitors. By targeting 14 trade partners simultaneously, the policy threatens to disrupt established global supply chains and elevate costs for importers. Export-heavy firms in India face the risk of reduced price competitiveness if these duty hikes are formally enacted.

Trade officials and policy experts are assessing options to respond to the proposed tariff structure. While formal negotiations may lie ahead, market observers are watching for potential diplomatic engagements to mitigate the impact. The development highlights how shifting geopolitical decisions can quickly reshape trade terms for emerging markets.
big_story.pullbox: Proposed US tariffs of up to 25% across 14 trade partners signal rising global trade protectionism, putting potential margin pressure on export-oriented Indian industries.

explains.title: What is a Tariff?
paragraphs: A tariff is a tax or duty imposed by a national government on goods and services imported from foreign countries. It is typically levied as a percentage of the declared value of the imported product as it crosses customs borders.

Governments implement tariffs to make foreign goods more expensive, thereby encouraging consumers to buy locally produced alternatives. While tariffs generate tax revenue and shield domestic businesses, they often increase consumer prices and invite retaliatory trade duties from foreign trade partners.

Indian chip design startup C2i Semiconductors has raised $15 million in a funding round led by Peak XV. Backed by the government's Design Linked Incentive (DLI) scheme, the deal marks the largest funding round ever recorded for an Indian semiconductor startup.

The capital injection will support the company's semiconductor design efforts as India accelerates its broader push toward domestic hardware capability. Peak XV's lead investment reflects rising venture funding interest in high-barrier deep-tech and hardware ventures across the domestic ecosystem.

story_1.headline: RBI Brings Gold Home as Food Price Pressures Persist
paragraphs: The Reserve Bank of India is actively bringing its gold reserves back home from overseas custody to strengthen domestic asset security. Concurrently, the central bank's latest monthly bulletin highlighted emerging broad-based food inflation pressures across the domestic economy.

Data from the bulletin also revealed that the RBI was a net dollar buyer in September. The monetary authority noted that global economic developments and shifts in US policy continue to influence Indian financial markets.

story_2.headline: Schaeffler AG to Offload ₹3,188 Crore Stake in Indian Arm
paragraphs: Schaeffler AG is set to sell a 6% stake in its listed Indian subsidiary Schaeffler India through a massive block deal valued at ₹3,188 crore. The floor price for the transaction has been set at ₹3,400 per share.
The proposed transaction comes amid a broader wave of promoter stake sales in corporate India, with LG Electronics India's promoter also considering a 2% stake sale worth ₹2,320.5 crore.

story_3.headline: Global Tech Stocks Slip as AI Rally Pauses
paragraphs: Global technology equities experienced renewed volatility as investor concerns over corporate AI spending and debt overshadow recent gains. The tech slide dragged major global indexes lower as enthusiasm over recent market rebounds began to cool.

geopolitics.headline: India and Egypt Target $12 Billion Bilateral Trade
paragraphs: India and Egypt have agreed to explore a preferential trade pact aimed at significantly expanding their commercial relationship. The two nations are targeting a total bilateral trade volume of USD 12 billion under the proposed framework. The agreement marks a strategic push by New Delhi to deepen economic and trade footprint across North Africa and the West Asia region.

While official discussions to structure the preferential trade deal are still at an exploratory stage, a formal pact could reduce tariff barriers for Indian exporters. However, key structural challenges remain around balancing bilateral trade gaps and aligning customs frameworks. For Indian businesses, enhanced trade access to Egypt provides a strategic gateway into wider African markets amid shifting global trade dynamics.

big_story.headline: Bio-Economy Target Set for $300 Million by 2030
big_story.text: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that India’s bio-economy is projected to reach 300 million Dollars by 2030, urging industry leaders to capitalize on the upcoming biotechnology revolution. The initiative aims to push sustainable innovation and green manufacturing across the country. This expansion strengthens India's global footprint in high-tech research and sustainable industrial growth.

big_story.headline: Tata Steel and APL Apollo Finalise ₹28,000-Crore Deal
big_story.text: Tata Steel has entered into a major ₹28,000-crore transaction with APL Apollo, restructuring key industrial assets to optimize market valuation and manufacturing capabilities. The deal focuses on enhancing operational efficiencies and expanding product reach in structural steel. This strategic consolidation underscores robust growth and capital allocation within India's manufacturing sector.

venture_vault.headline: SUK-M Secures Pre-Seed Funding for Thorium Microreactors
venture_vault.text: Deep-tech startup SUK-M has raised pre-seed funding led by Speciale Invest to accelerate the development of indigenous thorium microreactors. The capital will support advanced clean energy research aimed at providing safe and scalable power generation. This investment highlights India's push towards clean energy self-reliance and deep-tech innovation.

venture_vault.headline: Matters.AI Secures ₹115 Crore Funding for Enterprise Security
venture_vault.text: Cybersecurity startup Matters.AI has secured ₹115 crore in a Pre-Series A funding round to enhance its enterprise data security platform. The funds will be deployed to expand technology capabilities amidst growing enterprise demand for AI-driven data defense. The deal reflects rising investor trust in homegrown cybersecurity platforms protecting Indian businesses.

geopolitics.headline: India Sets Up Strategic Trade Command Centre for Trade Oversight
geopolitics.text: The Indian government has launched the National Strategic Trade Command Centre to enhance oversight and efficiency across the nation’s international trade ecosystem. The new authority will streamline regulatory frameworks, trade compliance, and export logistics. This structural reform aims to boost India's global trade governance and bolster export competitiveness.

geopolitics.headline: India-EU Free Trade Deal Scheduled for Brussels Signing on Dec 16
geopolitics.text: India and the European Union are set to sign a milestone free trade agreement on 16th December in Brussels following extensive bilateral negotiations. The deal aims to lower tariff barriers, boost market access, and deepen economic integration between India and the 27-member bloc. Secure trade access with Europe provides a major boost for Indian exporters.
